Gemini's voice picker orb transition
curationNote: Gemini's voice picker opens on a breathing gradient orb before resolving into a single card per voice — 'Vega, bright · higher voice' — that you swipe through one at a time. The orb-to-card handoff sells personality well: it signals a voice, not a setting, before you've heard anything. But swiping through options one by one instead of scanning a list means you can't compare two voices without holding both in memory — friction that doesn't pay for itself.

title: AI input mode switcher by Nitish Khagwal
curationNote: The quick-switch input pattern solves a real problem — AI tools need to handle multiple input modes (text, image gen, voice) without cluttering the interface. Nitish's approach keeps it to a single icon tap with a clean mode label, no tabs, no dropdowns. The animated text transition between modes — from 'Ask Anything' to 'Generate Image' — is the kind of micro-detail that makes a pattern feel production-ready rather than prototypey.

title: Cursor's agent task queue UI
curationNote: Cursor's hero leans on a kanban-style task queue — "In Progress" next to "Ready for Review" — the right metaphor for handing work to an agent instead of writing it yourself. Stacking a live CLI window over the browser preview shows the agent's reasoning without making you tab away. Worth knowing the pattern, but the shot itself is standard SaaS marketing chrome — nothing here pushes the UI forward.

title: Joyce's ambient agent summary concept
curationNote: Joyce treats the agent as ambient infrastructure rather than a chat window — one summary panel pulls highlights across Notion, Linear, Mail, Stripe and Calendar into a single feed instead of forcing you to open five apps. The blurred humanoid figure floating behind it is doing more conceptual lifting than the actual UI needs. The cross-app summarization pattern is the real idea here; the mood-board figure is the weak part.

title: Lué Studio's AI search section — scale your knowledge to ∞
curationNote: A website hero section for an AI knowledge base where a single answer bubble does the work that a paragraph of marketing copy usually fails at. Using a code snippet as the AI response example is the right call — it signals technical precision to a developer audience without the copy having to explain anything. Light palette and dot-grid background keep all attention on the interaction, not the chrome.

title: Muharrem Şenyıl's AI Oracle concept
curationNote: The 'AI oracle' framing is a bold conceptual move — it positions AI prediction as ritual rather than utility, which is a deliberate aesthetic choice that most AI products avoid. The name alone implies mystery and authority rather than helpfulness, which flips the usual AI UX script. This is a video demo: review the motion before publishing, the static thumbnail only tells half the story.

title: Oğuz Yağız Kara's monochrome UI work
curationNote: The 🤍🖤 framing is pure monochrome restraint — no colour, no decoration, contrast doing all the work. Kara consistently shows that black-and-white is a design decision, not a limitation. Review the image before publishing and update Tags to reflect the specific UI pattern shown.

title: Orior AI — Create Photorealistic UGC Characters & Post Everywhere
curationNote: AI-generated UGC influencers that are unsettlingly close to photoreal — the hard problem is keeping one face consistent across shots, and the hero image actually pulls that off. But the landing page undersells its own claim: a single static face, zero proof of range across angles or scenes. Worth trying if you're testing synthetic UGC for ad creative; not a must-have until they show more than one frame.

title: Semaloop's live 'SPEAKING' status overlay
curationNote: Semaloop's hero swaps the usual static dashboard mock for a live "SPEAKING" status pill pulsing over a phone screen — it shows the agent listening and acting instead of just promising it. That's the actual takeaway: the real-time status indicator is worth stealing for any voice or agent UI, regardless of what you're building. Worth trying if mobile QA is your bottleneck; the design itself isn't the product here.
